relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` touch any of the three things listed in `anchor.scope`: (1) the name of a command or installed entry point; (2) an install script, installer or install path; (3) a script, document, test or workflow that starts, runs or describes the console? Judge whether the item touches at least one of them. One deliverable or step anywhere in the item is enough, even when the rest of the item is about other work; an item whose only such step edits an install script, such as install.py, touches (2) even if it never mentions the console. Do not judge whether the item obeys `anchor.statement`.

criteria.yes: The item touches a command or entry-point name, an install script, installer or install path, or a script, document, test or workflow that starts, runs or describes the console.
criteria.no: The item touches none of the three: it changes something else, such as a message template, a data model or a review rule.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether it touches any of the three.

criteria.no: The item text is silent about the directive: it neither includes the directive's specific content nor references it.
criteria.unclear: The item text alludes to the directive's topic but it is not possible to tell whether the directive itself is included.
criteria.yes: The item text contains the directive's specific content, in its own words or the user's, as a step, constraint, or stated starting point.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly carry out, preserve, or plan for the directive given in `anchor.statement`? Look for the directive's specific content being present in the item: the same starting point, the same method, the same constraint, or an explicit step that does what the statement asks. A generic mention of the topic without the directive's specific content does not count. Judge presence of the directive only, not whether the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: The item text does not keep, add or run a hyphenated atm-bd-console command: it is silent about it, removes it, or names only the `atm-bd console` subcommand (with a space), the directory apps/atm-bd-console or the module atm_bd_console.
criteria.unclear: The item text refers to a console command but it is not possible to tell whether it means the hyphenated atm-bd-console command or the `atm-bd console` subcommand.
criteria.yes: The item text keeps, adds, aliases or runs a command named atm-bd-console (hyphenated), for example as an installed entry point, a console script, a compatibility alias, or a command line in a script, document, test or workflow.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` forbids one thing: a command named atm-bd-console (one hyphenated word) existing after installation, or any script, document, test or workflow running that hyphenated command. Decide whether `item.text` keeps, adds, aliases or runs that hyphenated atm-bd-console command. `atm-bd console`, written with a space, is a different command: the `console` subcommand of the `atm-bd` command; running, documenting or extending it is not a conflict. The directory apps/atm-bd-console and the Python module atm_bd_console are not the command either. Silence about atm-bd-console is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.
